spine: WHY accurate ideas lose when social incentives reward confident error; HOW distinguish equal dignity from conditional authority and propose a voluntary self-examining culture; WHAT metacult must protect criticism/fork/exit and distrustfounder, readintroandprotectionsagainstsuccess.
art: Copper and midnight community workroom: a loud lectern loses centrality as a shared evidence table gains an open review seat; the founder’s chair remains removable and the exit visibly usable. A voluntary culture is not pictured as a crowd worshipping an icon.
opening: Anti-Idiocracy argues that truth needs a culture capable of practicing correction.
A fast, confident error can defeat an explanation when the surrounding incentives reward performance.
The book proposes voluntary belonging that examines its own loyalties, leaders, and repeated practices.
Its provocative name for this social experiment is a metacult.
Readers are invited to judge whether shared identity can protect inquiry without becoming another authority trap.

spine: WHY apocalypse stories confuse disappearance of our familiar world with extinction; HOW separate hazard mechanisms/timescales from emotional certainty and examine distributed adaptivecapacity; WHAT survivalmaydegradefreedom so preserveknowledgecorrectionandplurality, readtitlenoteandfinalinheritancequestion.
art: Slate and sunrise-orange repair atelier: a damaged city model retains functioning knowledge/workshop pieces while a single master control seat stays empty; repair transfers an archive into a rebuilt structure. No exploding Earth, doomsday clock, or guaranteed rebirth.
opening: Why the World Won’t End offers conditional hope without claiming catastrophe is impossible.
It separates the end of a familiar world from the extinction of humanity.
The book takes serious hazards seriously while questioning the certainty that apocalypse stories encourage.
Its central concern is what a civilization must preserve so that learning can continue after disruption.
Readers gain a way to examine danger without confusing survival with a good future.
